name: Complete CLI and AI/CI operating protocol
scope: Freeze machine-readable command envelope and error model.
Freeze exit-code policy and mutation/query boundaries.
Demonstrate clean handoff workflow in a fresh process/chat-like environment.
out_of_scope: Concurrency hardening beyond current safe assumptions.

pre_execution_questions.question: Как выглядит canonical JSON envelope для всех CLI команд?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: AI integration становится хрупкой, если каждая команда возвращает произвольную форму.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Фиксируем ли единый набор exit codes?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: CI/AI должны различать usage error, verification failure and unresolved review.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: Yes. Recommended: 0 success/no blocking attention; 2 completed but attention/review required; 3 verification/domain validation failure; 4 usage/config error; 5 internal/runtime failure.
pre_execution_questions.answer: Yes. Recommended: 0 success/no blocking attention; 2 completed but attention/review required; 3 verification/domain validation failure; 4 usage/config error; 5 internal/runtime failure.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Какие команды строго read-only?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Это влияет на возможность безопасно исследовать проект перед изменениями.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: `status`, `diff`, `explain`, `history`, `graph`, `resources`, `verify` are read-only; `check`, `sync`, `rebuild`, `validate`, `materialize` may mutate runtime/generated state as documented.
pre_execution_questions.answer: `status`, `diff`, `explain`, `history`, `graph`, `resources`, and `verify` are read-only; `check`, `sync`, `rebuild`, `validate`, `materialize`, and `init` may mutate only the state/output documented for each command.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Freeze query/mutation boundaries in CLI contract and test them.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

pre_execution_questions.question: Нужно ли поддерживать stdin/stdout-only режим для агента?
pre_execution_questions.why_it_matters: Удобно для automation, но может расширить surface.
pre_execution_questions.recommended_default: JSON stdout is mandatory; structured stdin for bulk actions deferred unless a concrete use case appears.
pre_execution_questions.answer: JSON stdout is mandatory; structured stdin for bulk actions deferred unless a concrete use case appears.
pre_execution_questions.decision: Adopt this implementation default for v0.1 unless implementation evidence exposes a contradiction.
pre_execution_questions.acceptance_impact: Must be resolved before phase acceptance.

emergent_questions.question: Does freezing the Q6.1 envelope require a machine-output schema-version bump?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: The existing schema version 1.0.0 described a different top-level shape; silently reusing it would make AI/CI consumers unable to distinguish protocols.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Yes. Freeze the P6 canonical envelope as machine schema 2.0.0.
emergent_questions.answer: Yes. Freeze the P6 canonical envelope as machine schema 2.0.0.
emergent_questions.decision: Machine output schema is bumped from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0; the new top level is exactly `schema_version`, `command`, `ok`, `attention_required`, `data`, `warnings`, `errors`, `meta`.

emergent_questions.question: Can a read-only CLI command import project code if that import writes Python bytecode into the project?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: P6 declares verify/explain/graph and other queries read-only; creating `__pycache__` is still a project mutation.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. Project extension loading must suppress bytecode writes while preserving the caller process setting afterwards.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Project extension loading must suppress bytecode writes while preserving the caller process setting afterwards.
emergent_questions.decision: Project package import and lazy registration imports run with temporary `sys.dont_write_bytecode=True`; the previous global value is restored in `finally`.

emergent_questions.question: Which deterministic builders are independently required by `verify`?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Internal helper derived objects may legitimately have no documentation descriptor/standalone receipt, while documentation-owned derived outputs must be release-verifiable.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Release-gate documentation-owned derived descriptors and active recorded targets; do not require standalone receipts for internal-only helper builders.
emergent_questions.answer: Release-gate documentation-owned derived descriptors and active recorded targets; do not require standalone receipts for internal-only helper builders.
emergent_questions.decision: `verify` executes/checks managed `derived_descriptor` targets and persisted active receipts; internal-only helpers are verified transitively when required builders execute.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Avoids false release blockers while preserving required build evidence.

emergent_questions.question: Should `verify` fail fast when one project extension component is broken?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A complete report is more useful to CI/AI and the accepted verify semantics require reporting all available blocking findings rather than crashing at the first one.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. Load base builder/semantic components and renderer component separately; record component failures as findings and continue independent integrity/state checks.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Load base builder/semantic components and renderer component separately; record component failures as findings and continue independent integrity/state checks.
emergent_questions.decision: Verification aggregates component findings and continues dependency/state checks; renderer failure cannot erase persisted dependency diagnostics.

emergent_questions.question: Is the configured project Python package mandatory for `verify` on a documentation-only project?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: P1-P5 treat project code as optional when no code-owned semantics are needed; making verify require it would reject valid plain-Markdown projects.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: No. If the configured package directory is absent, verify uses empty builder/semantic registries and built-in renderers; actual derived/code-owned requirements still surface through resource evidence.
emergent_questions.answer: No. Documentation-only projects verify without creating a placeholder project package.
emergent_questions.decision: `verify` only loads the project package when it exists. Missing required builders are still reported for documentation-owned derived descriptors.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: DAX13/DAX17 domain-independent CLI behavior; resolved in P6.

emergent_questions.question: How should `verify` behave if the dependency runtime cannot even be constructed because its machine-owned root is unsafe/corrupt?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: A symlinked/unsafe `_dependency` tree is a verification finding, not an engine crash; fail-fast exit 5 loses the complete report contract.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Convert dependency-runtime construction failure into a blocking verification finding/section, continue independent checks, and return exit 3.
emergent_questions.answer: Verification now reports `dependency_runtime_unavailable` inside the complete report and continues independent builder/component checks where possible.
emergent_questions.decision: Domain corruption of dependency runtime is exit 3 verification evidence, not exit 5 internal failure.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Closes complete-report semantics for DAX12/DAX13/DAX14 and safety reporting for DAX04.

emergent_questions.question: May explicit project/documentation roots be nonexistent paths or regular files and still verify as an empty clean project?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Returning success for a nonexistent/file project root makes usage/config errors indistinguishable from a genuinely empty project.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Explicit project root must exist and be a directory; an existing documentation root must also be a directory. An absent documentation directory may represent an empty/uninitialized docs tree.
emergent_questions.answer: Root discovery now rejects nonexistent/non-directory project roots and existing non-directory documentation roots.
emergent_questions.decision: Invalid root shape is usage/config error (exit 4), never a clean verification success.

emergent_questions.question: Should accidental `SystemExit` from project imports/registration/builders/renderers be allowed to escape the machine protocol?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: Project-owned code can accidentally call `sys.exit`; if uncaught, `--json` produces stderr/process exit without the canonical envelope.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Catch `SystemExit` at project extension/builder/renderer boundaries and convert it into the same domain/component error classes; do not swallow `KeyboardInterrupt`.
emergent_questions.answer: Project import/registration/builder/renderer `SystemExit` is wrapped into engine domain/component errors and remains inside the JSON protocol.
emergent_questions.decision: Catch `SystemExit` specifically at project callback boundaries; cooperative code is still not sandboxed.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Closes DAX12/DAX13 machine-protocol escape without changing A1 trusted-code boundary.

emergent_questions.question: When a human CLI command fails or requires attention but already has structured diagnostic data, may the human renderer collapse it to only a status/roots line?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: P6-A1 requires human and JSON surfaces to expose the same underlying facts; hiding invalid targets makes the human surface non-diagnostic.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Render available command data for human failure/attention results as well as success, then append envelope issues.
emergent_questions.answer: Human dependency/orchestration output now preserves available diagnostic data on non-success; verify usage/config errors fall back to the generic issue renderer when no report exists.
emergent_questions.decision: Human output may summarize but must not discard the core diagnostic facts already present in `CommandResult.data`.

emergent_questions.question: How is the claimed CLI registry/parser parity protected against future drift?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: The P6 contract states acceptance tests compare the registry with parser surface, but the accepted v0.20 suite only checked the command set/envelope.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Add parser introspection regression coverage for command list, command-specific options and target cardinality, while checking the frozen exit table.
emergent_questions.answer: A dedicated P6 regression test now compares `CLI_COMMANDS.json` with the actual argparse surface and exit-code table.
emergent_questions.decision: Registry/parser parity is executable assurance rather than documentation-only intent.
emergent_questions.acceptance_impact: Closes DAX19/DAX20 assurance gap; runtime registry/parser already matched when probed.

emergent_questions.question: Should P6 verification reclassify a receipt with an unavailable semantic rule using only the old receipt dependency type?
emergent_questions.why_it_matters: P3/P4 canonical semantics treat `semantic_rule_unavailable` as invalid; calling it merely `review_required` makes verify disagree with runtime state semantics.
emergent_questions.recommended_default: Use the canonical invalidation rules: incomplete audit or unavailable source/builder/target/semantic rule is `invalid`; only inspectable structural changes use dependency-type-derived stale/review/build states.
emergent_questions.answer: Verification current-check classification now mirrors the canonical runtime semantics, including `semantic_rule_unavailable → invalid` and `audit_complete=false → invalid`.
emergent_questions.decision: Verify does not maintain a weaker parallel status classifier.

implementation_log.entry: Implemented canonical machine-output envelope schema 2.0.0 and stable exit codes 0/2/3/4/5.
Implemented read-only complete verification report over dependency integrity/current state, semantic review, required builders and materialization parity.
Converted argparse/usage and last-resort internal failures into canonical JSON envelopes when `--json` is requested.
Suppressed project-package bytecode writes so read-only commands preserve the project file tree.
Added fresh AI-style CLI-only workflow coverage from sync attention through semantic validation to successful verify.
acceptance correction: verify no longer requires an optional project package for plain documentation-only projects.
post-axis correction: verification dependency-runtime construction failures are blocking report findings rather than exit-5 internal failures.
post-axis correction: explicit project roots must exist/be directories and existing docs roots must be directories.
post-axis correction: project import/registration/builder/renderer SystemExit is wrapped into domain/component errors so JSON protocol remains intact.
post-axis correction: human non-success rendering preserves available diagnostic data and verify config errors surface issue text.
post-axis correction: verification status classification mirrors canonical invalid/unavailable semantics.
post-axis assurance: CLI registry/parser/target/exit table parity is now regression-tested; current registry matched the parser.
post-axis documentation correction: active materialization runtime documentation now identifies verify as implemented in P6.

findings: Machine protocol incompatibility is explicit through schema version 2.0.0; verification/report schemas are versioned and validated.
Explicit root shape is validated; unsafe dependency-runtime roots become verification findings rather than internal crashes.
Verify status classification now mirrors canonical invalidation semantics including semantic_rule_unavailable and incomplete audit evidence.
Verify reports unresolved semantic review as blocking evidence and never auto-accepts semantic validity.
Verify detects generated drift/missing/outdated/error/orphan state read-only and does not repair it.
All canonical command/error paths use stable 0/2/3/4/5 policy; read-only commands preserve engine-owned project file tree.
Project callback SystemExit no longer escapes the machine protocol; human non-success output retains diagnostic facts.
Fresh AI workflow reaches verify through CLI JSON only; canonical envelope is stable in installed-wheel smoke.
Invalid roots and project callback termination now remain machine-readable with stable exit classes.
Explain/history/integrity evidence remains available and verify aggregates component findings instead of fail-fast.
Complete verification survives dependency-runtime construction corruption and reports canonical semantic invalidation.
Historical incompatible envelope is not silently reused; machine schema is explicitly bumped to 2.0.0.
Full source and manifest-only portable regressions pass, including P0–P5 suites and dedicated P6 boundaries.
Registry/parser parity and post-acceptance failure modes now have explicit regression coverage.
Final post-axis docs and runtime build are synchronized at v0.21 / dev13.
Final dev13 wheel matches all 19 runtime Python modules in source.
Clean-venv protocol probes reproduce the corrected invalid-root, dependency-corruption and project-SystemExit behavior.
Manifest-only portable probe passes the full suite/spec audit with exact file set and hashes.

acceptance_summary.notes: P6 remains accepted after independent post-axis correction and final dev13 package gate. Confirmed verify/root/protocol/human-rendering/status-classification defects plus registry-test/documentation assurance gaps were corrected. Q6.E1–E11 are resolved implementer decisions; no unresolved blocking/user-owned question remains before P7.
